title: tau init --json output
description: Schema for the single JSON object `tau init [--json]` prints on stdout after writing (or overwriting with --force) the starter config. --stdout prints the JSONC scaffold itself instead of this object and is mutually exclusive with --json. --dry-run changes nothing: the same object gains "dry_run":true, an "action" summary, and a "files" array previewing every filesystem change including the exact JSONC body in files[].content (mutually exclusive with --stdout). New keys may be added (additive); existing keys keep their names and types.

config_path.description: Absolute path of the config file that was written, e.g. ~/.config/tau/config.json.

provider.description: Provider the scaffold was seeded for — an explicit --provider, else the first provider with a detected env key, else the default.

created.description: true when the run wrote a config file (always true on a successful write-path run).

overwritten.description: true when an existing config file was replaced via --force.

detected_env_keys.description: Names of the provider API-key environment variables found set on this machine (TAU_API_KEY included when the fallback is set). Values, never key material — only variable names.

dry_run.description: Present only under --dry-run: the object is a preview — no config file or directory was created and created/overwritten are always false.

action.description: Present only under --dry-run: what the run as spelled would do to config_path — "create" on a fresh path, "overwrite" when --force replaces an existing config.

files.description: Present only under --dry-run: every filesystem change the run would make, in order — the config dir (create_dir) only when it is missing, then the config file whose content is the exact JSONC body that would be written.

path.description: Absolute path the action applies to.

action.description: create_dir: mkdir -p the config dir; create: write a new file; overwrite: replace an existing file via --force.

format.description: Present on file entries: the body is JSONC (// and /* */ comments allowed).

content.description: Present on file entries: the exact bytes that would be written.
